claims.statement: From x ≤ y and the equation, 1/x + 1/y + 1/x + 1/x ≥ 1/2, hence 3/x ≥ 1/2 and x ≥ 3; also 1/x < 1/2 and 4/x ≥ 1/2, so x ≤ 8.

For fixed x, the y-interval is exactly y_min = floor( (1/2 - 1/x) / ( (3/2) - (1/x) ) ) + 1 and y_max = floor( 2 / ( (1/2) - (1/x) ) ), yielding the claimed intervals {7..18, 5..12, 5..10, 6..9, 7..8, 8}.
There are exactly 33 feasible (x,y) pairs, with per-x counts 12, 8, 6, 4, 2, 1 for x = 3,4,5,6,7,8 respectively.

For fixed feasible (x,y) with R = 1/2 - 1/x - 1/y, the residual equation is 1/z + 1/w = R. Since z ≤ w, 1/z ≥ R/2 and 1/z ≤ R, giving max(y, floor(1/R)+1) ≤ z ≤ floor(2/R), with the left inequality floor(1/R)+1 arising from 1/z > R and the right from 1/z ≥ R/2.
For reduced R = a/b, the equation 1/z + 1/w = a/b with z ≤ w is equivalent to (az-b)(aw-b) = b², where z = (d+b)/a and w = (e+b)/a for a factor pair de = b².
The bijection between solutions (z,w) and factor pairs (d,e) of b² satisfies d ≡ -b (mod a) and d ≤ e iff z ≤ w; the condition z ≥ y is an additional modular-arithmetic filter on the factor pairs.
For each feasible (x,y) in the 33-pair skeleton, the reduced residual a/b and integer b² can be computed in exact rational arithmetic, giving a complete auditable table of z-intervals.
The dossier contains no independent computational artifact or second source that could conflict with the derived bounds; the only source is the problem statement.
